ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with distinct dark spots and a pale snout. It features a granular dorsum and a characteristic high-pitched, insect-like call. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes tinniens* is best distinguished by the prominent, distinct white spots scattered across its dark, granular dorsal skin, which contrast sharply with its body.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes tinniens* inhabits high-altitude montane evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of high-altitude shrubbery.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes tinniens* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in vegetation or tree holes.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes tinniens* is endemic to the high-altitude shola grasslands and forests of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Spotted Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like series of rapid, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude montane forests.
